di_francesco_2024.plan: Here we performed an extensive assessment of graded levels of caloric restriction (20% and 40%) and intermittent fasting (1 and 2 days fasting per week) on the health and survival of 960 genetically diverse female mice.
di_francesco_2024.debut: Feeding schedules for DR were started at 6 months of age.
di_francesco_2024.mediane_40: 40% CR mice achieved a median lifespan of around 9 months (36.3%) greater than mice in the AL group.
di_francesco_2024.cout: 40% caloric restriction had the strongest lifespan extension effect but led to a loss of lean mass and changes in the immune repertoire that could confer susceptibility to infections.

calerie_waziry_2023.restriction_obtenue: most participants achieving doses below the prescribed 25% (mean = 11.9, s.e.m. = 0.7%)
calerie_waziry_2023.effectifs: for n = 197 participants (128 CR and 69 AL)
calerie_waziry_2023.traduction: Standardized treatment effects on DunedinPACE correspond to a reduction in the pace of aging of 2–3%.
calerie_waziry_2023.effet_20_pourcent: the effect of 20% CR on DunedinPACE was d = −0.43 (95% CI −0.67, −0.19) at 12 months and d = −0.40 (95% CI −0.67, −0.12) at 24 months
calerie_waziry_2023.mortalite_extrapolee: the CALERIE treatment effect of 2–3% slower pace of aging corresponds to a reduction in mortality risk of as much as 10–15%
calerie_waziry_2023.note_d_retenu: 0,27 : moyenne des effets à 12 et 24 mois (0,29 et 0,25) ; 0,43 : effet à 12 mois pour 20 % de restriction.

mattison_2017.reference: Mattison et al., Nature Communications 2017;8:14063, doi:10.1038/ncomms14063 (PMC5247583)
mattison_2017.resume: The University of Wisconsin study reported a significant positive impact of CR on survival, but the National Institute on Aging study detected no significant survival effect.
